---

### Data Presentation

| Metric | Current Value | Baseline / Target | Delta (%) | Status (Normal/Warning/Critical) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Bank Float Voltage (Total)** | 133.80 V DC | 132.00 – 135.00 V DC (2.23 V/cell) | +1.36% | **Normal** |
| **Min. Cell Float Voltage** | 2.21 V DC | $\ge$ 2.14 V DC (IEEE 450 low limit) | +3.27% | **Normal** |
| **Max. Cell Float Voltage** | 2.24 V DC | $\le$ 2.28 V DC (IEEE 450 high limit) | -1.75% | **Normal** |
| **Avg. Internal Cell Resistance** | 185.0 $\mu\Omega$ | 180.0 $\mu\Omega$ (Factory Baseline) | +2.78% | **Normal** |
| **Max. Internal Resistance Delta** | +12.5% (Cell #42) | $< 20.0\%$ (Warning: $+20\%$, Action: $+50\%$) | N/A | **Normal** |
| **Intercell Connection Resistance** | 11.2 $\mu\Omega$ avg | $\le 15.0\ \mu\Omega$ ($<20\%$ above baseline) | +4.67% | **Normal** |
| **Electrolyte Temperature** | 23.8 °C (74.8 °F) | 25.0 °C (77.0 °F Nominal) | -4.80% | **Normal** |
| **Asset Health Index (AHI)** | 92.4 / 100 | $\ge 85.0$ | +8.71% | **Normal** |

- **Temperature Compensation Verification**: Ensure DC charger temperature compensation coefficient remains calibrated to -3.0 mV/°C/cell relative to the standard 25°C baseline.

input: Track the thermal runaway risk and electrolyte level degradation across lead-acid banks over the trailing 12 months.

**Across the fleet of lead-acid substation battery banks over the trailing 12 months, thermal runaway risk peaked during high ambient summer months driven by elevated float currents and internal cell impedance buildup, while electrolyte levels exhibited a steady 26.0% degradation across unmaintained flooded cells. Fleet-wide Asset Health Index (AHI) currently averages 71.4%, with 8 banks in Warning status and 2 banks breaching Critical IEEE 450/1188 operational limits due to severe dry-out and float current instability. Immediate electrolyte replenishment, temperature-compensated charger calibration, and targeted impedance testing are required to mitigate catastrophic cell dry-out and thermal runaway.**

input: What is the probability of DC trip failure on transmission breakers during an AC station service blackout?
expected_output:
### Executive Summary
**Under standard IEEE 485 sizing and NERC PRC-005-6 compliance, the conditional probability of a transmission breaker DC trip failure during an AC station service blackout is between 0.02% and 0.50% ($2.0 \times 10^{-4}$ to $5.0 \times 10^{-3}$) for a healthy station battery system within its 8-hour duty cycle. However, if the station battery system exhibits advanced degradation (Asset Health Index $< 70$, internal cell impedance $> 150\%$ of baseline, or float voltage collapse under peak inrush), this failure probability surges non-linearly to 18.5%–32.5% during extended discharge. The primary root causes of failure during AC loss are sudden DC bus voltage sag under breaker trip coil inrush ($10\text{--}30\text{ A}$ instantaneous per coil), depleted ampere-hour capacity, and unmonitored open-circuit inter-cell resistance.**

---

### Quantitative Reliability & Component Failure Breakdown

The following reliability assessment models the probability of DC trip failure on a standard $125\text{ VDC} / 250\text{ VDC}$ substation protection and control system following total loss of AC station service (chargers de-energized, batteries supporting all continuous standing and non-continuous momentary trip loads):

| Metric | Current Value | Baseline / Target | Delta (%) | Status (Normal/Warning/Critical) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Composite Trip Failure Probability (Dual Bank, AHI $\ge$ 90)** | $0.05\%$ ($5.0 \times 10^{-4}$) | $\le 0.08\%$ | $-37.5\%$ | **Normal** |
| **Composite Trip Failure Probability (Single Bank, Nominal)** | $0.35\%$ ($3.5 \times 10^{-3}$) | $\le 0.50\%$ | $-30.0\%$ | **Normal** |
| **Trip Failure Probability (Degraded Battery Bank, AHI $< 70$)** | $19.80\%$ ($1.98 \times 10^{-1}$) | $\le 0.50\%$ | $+3860.0\%$ | **Critical** |
| **End-of-Discharge Bus Voltage (8-Hour Blackout Peak Trip)** | $105.2\text{ VDC}$ | $\ge 105.0\text{ VDC}$ ($1.75\text{ VPC}$) | $+0.19\%$ | **Warning** |
| **Internal Cell Resistance ($R_{\text{int}}$ / Impedance Drift)** | $1.42\text{ m}\Omega$ | $\le 1.10\text{ m}\Omega$ ($<20\%$ rise) | $+29.1\%$ | **Warning** |
| **Trip Circuit Supervision (TCS) Continuity Availability** | $99.92\%$ | $\ge 99.99\%$ | $-0.07\%$ | **Normal** |
| **DC Ground Fault Latency / Sensitivity Margin** | $2.8\text{ k}\Omega$ | $> 10.0\text{ k}\Omega$ | $-72.0\%$ | **Warning** |

*Assumptions: Lead-Acid (VLA/VRLA) IEEE 485 discharge curve, 8-hour rated duty cycle, ambient temperature $25^\circ\text{C}$, 2-breaker simultaneous trip event ($25\text{ A}$ inrush each) at end of discharge envelope.*

---

### Reliability Dynamics & Failure Modes

1. **Terminal Voltage Collapse During Trip Inrush**: Breaker trip coils draw momentary inductive currents ($10\text{--}30\text{ A}$ per coil for $50\text{--}100\text{ ms}$). When the battery bank is operating on deep discharge with degraded internal plate conductance, terminal voltage sags below relay dropout levels ($\approx 80\text{ VDC}$ on a $125\text{ VDC}$ system), preventing trip latch disengagement.
2. **Duty-Cycle Depletion & Temperature Derating**: Low ambient substation temperatures ($< 0^\circ\text{C}$) reduce available chemical capacity by up to $20\text{--}30\%$, causing premature voltage cutoff well before the nominal 8-hour reserve margin is reached.
3. **Common-Mode DC Ground Faults**: Unresolved DC cross-trip grounds or negative-polarity ground faults can bypass trip contacts or induce control fuse blowouts during fault clearing sequences.

---

### Visualization: Blackout Duration vs. Trip Failure Probability

```json
{
  "chart_type": "line",
  "title": "DC Trip Failure Probability vs. Station Blackout Duration",
  "xAxis": "Blackout Duration (Hours)",
  "yAxis": "Failure Probability (%)",
  "series": [
    {
      "name": "Healthy Dual Bank (AHI > 90)",
      "data": [0.02, 0.03, 0.05, 0.08, 0.15, 0.45, 1.2, 3.8]
    },
    {
      "name": "Single Bank Baseline (AHI 80-89)",
      "data": [0.25, 0.35, 0.55, 0.95, 1.8, 4.2, 11.5, 28.0]
    },
    {
      "name": "Degraded Bank (AHI < 70)",
      "data": [5.2, 7.8, 12.4, 19.8, 32.5, 54.0, 78.5, 95.0]
    }
  ],
  "categories": ["0h", "1h", "2h", "4h", "6h", "8h", "10h", "12h"]
}
```

---

### Actionable Recommendations

- **Prioritize PRC-005 Battery Impedance & Discharge Capacity Testing**: Conduct immediate modified capacity discharge tests (IEEE 450/1188) on any station battery bank with internal ohmic values exhibiting $>20\%$ deviation from initial baseline.
- **Enforce Continuous Battery Monitoring Systems (BMS)**: Implement online cell-level voltage, temperature, and string internal resistance telemetry with real-time alerting for DC bus sags during routine switching.
- **Validate Trip Circuit Supervision (TCS) Alarms**: Ensure dual trip coil circuits (Trip 1 / Trip 2) are powered from independent DC distribution boards/fuses to eliminate single-point DC supply failure.
- **Implement Non-Essential DC Load Shedding**: During confirmed AC station service outages exceeding 2 hours, automatically shed non-critical DC loads (substation emergency lighting, continuous communication auxiliary heaters) to preserve trip reserve capacity.
